body_text: View All News American Integrity Surpasses 40,000 LinkedIn Followers, Reflecting Industry Leadership and Stakeholder Engagement July 30, 2026 Download (opens in new window) Growing audience recognizes American Integrity’s trusted voice on insurance and leadership, while celebrating its employee culture, community impact, and commitment to serving policyholders, independent agents, investors, employees, and communities across the property insurance industry. TAMPA, Fla.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- American Integrity Insurance Group, Inc. (NYSE: AII) (“American Integrity,” “we,” “us,” “our,” or the “Company”), a Tampa-based property and casualty insurance holding company and one of Florida’s leading providers of residential property insurance, today announced that it has reached a significant milestone on LinkedIn, surpassing 40,000 followers, reflecting continued engagement with policyholders, independent agents, employees, investors, and the broader property insurance community. While follower counts often measure popularity, American Integrity views the achievement as a reflection of the relationships the Company has built with policyholders, independent agents, employees, stockholders, community partners, and others who have chosen to engage with its story. "For us, this accomplishment isn't about social media," said Bob Ritchie, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of American Integrity. "It's about trust. Every person who follows American Integrity has chosen to connect with our company, our people, and our mission. We don't see 40,000 followers – we see 40,000 relationships, and we're incredibly grateful for each and every one of them." American Integrity has cultivated a LinkedIn community that rivals—and in many cases exceeds—organizations many times its size by consistently sharing meaningful content that educates, informs, and celebrates the people, partnerships, and purpose behind the business. Rather than focusing solely on insurance products and services, the Company's content strategy emphasizes customer stories, employee recognition, community involvement, leadership insights, educational resources, industry expertise, and events that provide a behind-the-scenes look at the organization's culture and mission. The Company's digital presence has become an extension of its broader mission to lead with integrity, transparency, and service. "Our goal has never been to chase algorithms or viral moments," Mr. Ritchie added. "We've simply tried to tell authentic stories about the people who make American Integrity what it is. When organizations consistently lead with authenticity, people respond." Since launching its renewed brand strategy, American Integrity has continued to expand its digital presence while strengthening relationships across the insurance industry and the communities it serves. The Company believes thoughtful communication, transparency, and authentic storytelling help build lasting trust with all of its stakeholders. Mr. Ritchie continued, "Forty thousand followers isn't the story. The story is what those 40,000 people represent—trust, connection, and a shared belief in who we are and where we're going. We're honored they've chosen to be part of our journey." As American Integrity looks ahead, the Company remains committed to sharing the stories that matter most while continuing to educate, engage, and strengthen relationships with policyholders, independent agents, investors, employees, and the communities it serves. About American Integrity Insurance Group, Inc. American Integrity Insurance Group, Inc. (NYSE: AII) is a leading provider of residential property insurance, focused on delivering innovative, reliable coverage to homeowners throughout the Southeast. Built on a foundation of integrity, resilience, and service, the Company’s mission is to be the most trusted and responsive insurance solution in the markets it serves. Founded in 2006 and headquartered in Tampa, American Integrity is committed to protecting policyholders with strength and purpose—today and for generations to come. For more information, visit www.aii.com and follow the Company on LinkedIn . Media Contact: Toni Logan American Integrity Insurance Group, Inc. tlogan@aii.com 813-240-7607 Source: American Integrity Insurance Group, Inc. View All News

title: SRX Global Reports Paper-Traded EMJX Return of ~25% Since February 11, 2026

body_text: SRX Global Reports Paper-Traded EMJX Return of ~25% Since February 11, 2026 July 14, 2026 9:20am EDT EMJX Shifted from “Stress” to “Mixed” for Bitcoin Company Files Updated Investor Presentation Outlining Performance and Strategy Management to Host Fireside Chat Today at 10:30am ET NORTH PALM BEACH, Fla., July 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SRX Global Inc. (NYSE American: SRXH) (the “Company”, or “SRX”), an AI-enabled platform dedicated to generating returns across high-conviction operating companies and assets, today reported paper-traded EMJX returns of 26% from February 11, 2026 to July 10, 2026. The EMJX model reads market regime across three states — Bull, Mixed, and Stress — updating every trading day with a forward read on where crypto is heading over roughly the next 30 days. That signal is now available as an institutional product to a select group of clients — digital-asset treasuries, miners, and funds that are structurally long crypto and need a disciplined way to anticipate the next major move and manage risk. Since February 11, 2026, the EMJX strategy has run as a paper-traded portfolio (no actual investments were made and no capital has been deployed) ahead of the acquisition by SRX Global. It is a full Gen2 crypto treasury: Bitcoin, Ethereum, altcoins, high-convexity tech equities (such as OPEN), and options. Following the acquisition, SRX will begin trading the strategy with real capital in a fully auditable way, and is pursuing additional discussions to bring the system to market in a form that would be accessible to investors. Paper-Traded EMJX Results 1 February 11 – July 10, 2026 (149 days): Total return: +24.8% (time-weighted) versus Bitcoin -4.2% over the same period — a spread of roughly 29 points Outperformed all 4 crypto-treasury comparables at 30 days, 60 days, and since inception. EMJX vs. crypto-treasury comps — hypothetical cumulative return since inception Investor fireside chat — Tuesday, July 14, 2026, 10:30 a.m. ET. Eric Jackson will host, along with Kent Cunningham, SRX Global’s CEO, a live fireside chat with investors to discuss the regime shift, the track record, and what comes next. Register here . 1 Performance disclosure: These results are from a paper-traded portfolio. Every trade was a real, forward-looking decision — recorded and emailed in advance each trading morning to a member of the SRXH board, marked to actual market prices, kept within margin requirements and net of broker costs. It is not a simulation or a backtest. However, no actual capital was deployed, so it does not represent live trading with real money; results achieved with deployed capital may differ, including from execution, liquidity, slippage, financing, and market-impact effects a paper book does not fully capture. Past performance does not guarantee future results. Nothing herein is investment advice or an offer or solicitation to buy or sell any security, digital asset, or fund interest. The Company leverages proprietary technology, data analytics, and disciplined capital allocation to identify and manage investments across multiple sectors. title: Gladstone Investment Corporation Expands Its Investment in Global GRAB Technologies Through the Acquisition of RSSI Barriers
body_text: Gladstone Investment Corporation Expands Its Investment in Global GRAB Technologies Through the Acquisition of RSSI Barriers Download as PDF July 20, 2026 8:30am EDT MCLEAN, VA / ACCESS Newswire / July 20, 2026 / Gladstone Investment Corporation (Nasdaq:GAIN) ("Gladstone Investment") is pleased to announce that it has continued its support of portfolio company Global GRAB Technologies, Inc. ("Global GRAB") through providing additional capital to support the acquisition of substantially all of the assets of RSSI Barriers, LLC ("RSSI"). Global GRAB, headquartered in Franklin, Tennessee, is a leading provider of physical perimeter security and hostile vehicle mitigation solutions serving military installations, government facilities, critical infrastructure, transportation, utility, commercial and other high-security environments. RSSI is a well-recognized market leader and industry pioneer in 100% electric crash-rated barrier technology and solutions for gate automation. RSSI's electric barrier systems have successfully undergone rigorous crash testing and certification standards and are trusted by customers responsible for protecting mission-critical facilities. Global GRAB and RSSI have partnered for years to deliver innovative security solutions across high-security end markets. The acquisition represents a natural evolution of that relationship and meaningfully expands Global GRAB's portfolio of engineered and crash-certified perimeter security solutions. Together, Global GRAB and RSSI will offer customers a broader suite of crash-rated vehicle barriers, less-than-lethal technologies, perimeter reinforcement systems, intelligent detection solutions, integrated access control products, and lifecycle support capabilities. "Global GRAB Technologies has collaborated with RSSI on various opportunities and projects for years and has formed a great partnership," said Brian Cooper, COO and President of Global GRAB. "We're excited to bring RSSI into the Global GRAB family of brands and continue delivering innovative security solutions to our customers." "This acquisition is about more than expanding our product portfolio," said Mark Horne, Chief Executive Officer of Global GRAB. "It brings together two organizations with a shared commitment to innovation, engineering excellence and protecting people, critical infrastructure and national assets. By combining our expertise, we are better positioned than ever to deliver comprehensive perimeter security solutions that address today's evolving threats." "RSSI is a highly strategic acquisition for Global GRAB and reinforces the platform's position as a leading provider of mission-critical perimeter security and hostile vehicle mitigation solutions," said Michael Cueter, Managing Director at Gladstone Investment. "RSSI brings a well-recognized brand, differentiated electric crash-rated barrier technology, and deep customer credibility in demanding security environments. We are excited to continue supporting the Global GRAB team as they expand the platform's capabilities, product breadth and ability to serve customers protecting critical infrastructure and national assets." Gladstone Investment is a publicly traded business development company that seeks to make equity and secured debt investments in lower middle market businesses in connection with acquisitions, changes in control, and recapitalizations. Additional information on the transaction can be found at www.gladstoneinvestment.com . For Investor Relations inquiries related to any of the monthly dividend paying Gladstone funds, please visit www.gladstone.com . title: [Toyota Times] Former Japan National Soccer Team Coach Okada Visits Toyota Technical Skills Academy: Lessons for Life
summary: Takeshi Okada, former head coach of the Japanese national soccer team, held a special class at Toyota Technical Skills Academy. What did this legendary coach, someone who knows what it takes to compete on the world stage, share with these students? #TOYOTATIMES
body_text: Takeshi Okada, former head coach of the Japanese national soccer team, held a special class at Toyota Technical Skills Academy. What did this legendary coach, someone who knows what it takes to compete on the world stage, share with these students? Takeshi Okada is the former head coach of Japan's national soccer team and current principal of FC Imabari High School Satoyama in Ehime Prefecture. His teaching philosophy resonated with Chairman Akio Toyoda, leading to a bond that has been given shape in “ Akio Juku ,” a special lecture held at the school. Okada hosted the “Okada Juku” in return. Okada toured the school prior to the session, saying “I want to share something that might help them, even if just a little, as they make their way through life.” How did he deal with his players as a coach under the pressure of competing on the world stage? What does it take to grow, how do you build a strong organization, what values does he hold dear...? The students hung on his every word, all based in experience. Different though soccer and manufacturing may be, the students appeared to sense a common thread. What did this legendary coach share with the young people who will shape the future of manufacturing? The “Okada Juku” kicks off! facebook X（formerly Twitter）

title: Luxfer Declares Quarterly Dividend
body_text: Luxfer Declares Quarterly Dividend 6 July 2026 RIVERSIDE, California, July 6, 2026 – (BUSINESS WIRE) – Luxfer Holdings PLC (NYSE: LXFR) (“Luxfer” or the “Company”), a global industrial company innovating niche applications in materials engineering, today announced that its Board of Directors declared a quarterly dividend of 13 cents per ordinary share. The dividend will be payable on August 5, 2026 to shareholders of record as of the close of business on July 17, 2026. About Luxfer Holdings PLC Luxfer is a global industrial company innovating niche applications in materials engineering. Using its broad array of proprietary technologies, Luxfer focuses on value creation, customer satisfaction, and demanding applications where technical know-how and manufacturing expertise combine to deliver a superior product. Luxfer’s high-performance materials, components, and high-pressure gas containment devices are used in defense and emergency response, clean energy, healthcare, transportation, and general industrial applications. Luxfer is listed on the New York Stock Exchange and its ordinary shares trade under the symbol LXFR. title: Australian Authorities Reject Claims of Horse Meat Found in Food Products, Defend Food Safety Standards

body_text: Food safety has once again become a topic of public debate in Australia after claims emerged that horse meat had been detected in products intended for human consumption. The allegations, raised in an investigative report citing confidential government documents, sparked widespread concern among consumers. However, Australian authorities have strongly denied the claims, insisting that there is no evidence horse meat has been found in beef, lamb, or any other food sold for people to eat. The dispute has reignited discussions about food safety oversight, regulatory transparency, and consumer confidence in Australia's food supply. While lawmakers have called for greater accountability, the New South Wales (NSW) government maintains that existing surveillance and enforcement measures are working effectively. Claims of Horse Meat Spark Public Concern The controversy began after an investigative report alleged that confidential documents obtained through parliamentary powers indicated horse meat had been detected in food products meant for human consumption. The report suggested that some consumers may have unknowingly purchased or consumed products marketed as beef or lamb that contained horse meat. The investigation also questioned whether Australia's food regulator had been sufficiently transparent about food safety breaches and contamination incidents. The claims quickly attracted national attention, particularly because they echoed memories of the 2013 European horse meat scandal, during which horse DNA was discovered in products labelled as beef across several countries. NSW Government Rejects the Allegations In response to the report, the New South Wales Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development (DPIRD) issued a statement firmly rejecting the allegations. According to the department, the NSW Food Authority has not found horse meat in beef, lamb, or any food intended for human consumption. Officials described the claims as misleading and stated that routine surveillance testing has not identified horse meat in products sold to consumers. The department emphasized that species identification testing is regularly conducted on meat products as part of its food safety monitoring program. Authorities say these tests are designed to detect mislabeling or food fraud, and no incidents involving horse meat in food for human consumption have been recorded. Parliamentary Documents Raise Broader Food Safety Questions The investigation relied on confidential documents reportedly obtained by NSW Greens MP Abigail Boyd through parliamentary procedures. While many of the documents cannot be publicly released, Boyd said they highlighted numerous food safety incidents involving contaminants that should never appear in food products. Examples reportedly included: Mouse fur found in food. Metal shavings discovered in bread products. Products labelled as dairy-free that allegedly contained dairy. Other contamination incidents identified after consumers became ill. Claims that needles had been found in food in certain cases. Boyd argued that these incidents demonstrate weaknesses in Australia's food safety enforcement system and suggested consumers may place too much trust in regulatory oversight. She also expressed concern that food safety issues are not always identified by manufacturers themselves, but sometimes only after consumers report illnesses or contamination. Authorities Clarify the Horse Meat Issue Although the investigation referenced horse meat, NSW authorities stressed that the claim does not reflect the findings of official investigations. Officials explained that horse meat can legally be sold for human consumption in Australia if it is processed at a licensed abattoir that meets strict regulatory standards. However, the department noted that there are currently no licensed horse meat processing abattoirs in New South Wales for human food production. Authorities further clarified that the investigation referenced illegal knackeries, which process animal carcasses for pet food rather than food intended for people. This distinction is important because meat processed for animal feed follows a completely different regulatory pathway than meat entering the human food supply. Illegal Knackery Investigation Explained The department said part of the investigation focused on an illegal knackery operating in Wagga Wagga. According to officials, meat processed at the facility was intended primarily for pet food, particularly for the greyhound racing industry, rather than for supermarkets or food retailers serving consumers. The operator, Adrian Talbot, was convicted of operating an unlicensed knackery and an unlicensed animal food transport vehicle. Court proceedings resulted in financial penalties, including fines and legal costs. Authorities say the case demonstrates enforcement action against illegal operations rather than evidence that contaminated meat entered Australia's human food chain. Food Safety Surveillance in Australia Australian food regulators conduct regular inspections, laboratory testing, and compliance monitoring throughout the food supply chain. Routine surveillance includes testing meat products to verify species identification and detect potential food fraud. These programs are designed to identify: Mislabelled meat products. Contamination. Undeclared allergens. Food safety hazards. Regulatory violations. Authorities argue that ongoing monitoring helps maintain consumer confidence while identifying businesses that fail to meet food safety standards. Why Horse Meat Is Such a Sensitive Issue Although horse meat is legally consumed in several countries, including parts of Europe and Asia, many consumers in Australia and the United Kingdom strongly associate horses with companion or sporting animals rather than food. As a result, allegations involving undeclared horse meat often generate significant public concern even when there is limited evidence. The issue also raises broader questions about food fraud, accurate labelling, and consumer rights. If meat products are intentionally mislabelled, consumers lose the ability to make informed purchasing decisions based on dietary preferences, cultural beliefs, allergies, or ethical considerations. Memories of the 2013 Horse Meat Scandal The latest controversy has drawn comparisons with the major European horse meat scandal uncovered in 2013. During that investigation, DNA testing revealed horse meat in products marketed as beef, including frozen meals, burgers, and lasagne sold across several European countries, including the United Kingdom. The incident prompted extensive reforms to food traceability systems, supply chain monitoring, and DNA testing requirements throughout Europe. Although Australian authorities insist the current allegations are unrelated and unsupported by official testing, the earlier scandal continues to influence public perceptions whenever similar claims emerge. Consumer Confidence Remains Central The disagreement between investigators and government authorities highlights the importance of transparency in food regulation. Consumers generally expect food labels to accurately describe what they are purchasing and rely on regulators to ensure safety standards are consistently enforced. While officials maintain there is no evidence horse meat has entered Australia's human food supply, the broader discussion has renewed calls for continued oversight, transparent reporting, and robust food testing programs. As investigations and political debate continue, Australian regulators maintain that current evidence supports the integrity of the state's food safety system.
